label: no
controls_available: Six visible ingredient jars; click to load or replace an ingredient through jar_select.
Fifteen visible curve-notch buttons; click notch 1 through 15 through grind_set (internal steps 0 through 14).
STIR PATH; each click advances the selected constant-curvature path synchronously by six of 24 samples, and repeated clicks complete a route segment.
WATER; up to five synchronous recovery moves of at most 30 px toward the origin.
BELLOWS; up to three synchronous moves of 19 px along the current heading.
SEAL; click to submit the replay once the route and target effect are complete.
Jar dragging and duration-based pestle holding are unavailable in the simplified interface; those are full-only controls.
autonomous_processes: Idle waiting during any simplified action opportunity causes no outcome-affecting task-state change; position, heading, selection, notch, path index, route progress, revealed trace, hazard contacts, vortex contacts, and budgets remain fixed, so the same controls retain the same state-dependent availability.

Path traversal, vortex displacement, hazard contact, reveal, and exposure of the next route gate all occur synchronously inside a STIR PATH, WATER, or BELLOWS handler; there is no autonomous continuation after the click.
The 240 ms grind-tick requestAnimationFrame process is full-only: simplified startGrinding returns immediately and the pestle is disabled, so it is not active in this configuration.
After a failed seal, the 1.8 second timeout only removes the fresh-failure presentation; it does not change route, position, or any other outcome-affecting state.
grouped_control_modes: Ingredient selection/replacement via visible jar clicks (load_ingredient and replace_ingredient, input_source=jar_select).
Curve-notch selection via all fifteen visible notch buttons (grind_set, input_source=curve_notches).
STIR PATH clicks (stir, input_source=ladle_click), including every repeated path-advance occurrence.

clause_i.reason: As a static information subcondition, an observation-free policy is not uniformly optimal across the generated worlds: the same initial action history can face different shuffled ingredients, route schedules, and path geometry, so I_t alone cannot select the seed-specific jar/notch choice. This does not supply time dependence.

clause_ii.reason: As a static visual subcondition, the current screenshot renders the ordered target, current route ring, selected-ingredient path preview, notch state, position, and revealed trace; a screenshot-only policy can choose the next static click from the endpoint frame. One frame is sufficient for this purpose, consistent with frames_per_observation=1. It does not predict an autonomous evolution.

clause_iii.reason: No legitimate grouped control mode has a non-clock autonomous state evolution in simplified mode. Stir and recovery motion, reveal, route progress, and collisions are completed inside the input handler; waiting leaves the model state unchanged. The only timed pestle animation is gated to full interaction, and the post-failure timeout is presentation-only. Therefore waiting cannot produce the required strict Q loss (apart from the definition's excluded deadline/later-completion effect), and no choice of Delta or w repairs this failure.

common_visible_process: None. Seed-dependent static geometry makes observation useful, but it does not evolve autonomously. The full-only pestle animation and the post-failure overlay timeout are separate from the simplified outcome process and cannot witness clauses (i), (ii), and (iii) together.

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already fails clause (iii), so the pre-run threshold cannot change the catalog label. The exact simplified configuration has no autonomous outcome phase: a successful normal UI solution must continue sending outcome-affecting selection, notch, path, and recovery clicks.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 sets six ingredients, five dependent route commits, fifteen notches, three vortices, no tolerated bone contact, and the listed recovery budgets; simplified is jar selection plus discrete curve-notch buttons; the observation window is 240 ms with one frame.
The generator consumes the injected control condition's difficulty_parameters rather than a fixed difficulty, so the assigned difficulty-5 values are the active world parameters.

Route choices and geometry are generated from a seed and shuffled/randomized into fixed ingredient/path records; the mechanic constants are fixed path samples, synchronous stir stride, and a grind tick value, with no autonomous world schedule.
The simplified branch enables notch buttons and jar clicks, updates selection synchronously, disables the full-only pestle, and binds STIR, WATER, BELLOWS, and SEAL as direct handlers.
Duration-based grinding and requestAnimationFrame grind ticks are explicitly guarded by interaction === full; simplified cannot enter this process.
STIR and recovery actions calculate motion, collisions, reveals, route progress, and budgets within the same event handler and then redraw; there is no idle continuation.
The only mechanic timeout is a post-failure 1.8 second removal of the fresh-failure overlay/readout, not an outcome-state transition.
The only keyframe animation is the pestle animation under data-grinding=true, while simplified makes the pestle inactive/default; this animation is not part of the assigned mode.

The grader binds ingredient loading and grind_set to simplified input sources and replays stir, water, bellows, and seal events synchronously from the submitted event list; it has no event-time or idle-evolution rule.
Verification only loads the exported result and invokes the deterministic replay grader; it adds no timing-dependent task behavior.

The shared clock controls queued timers and animation-frame callbacks during live versus paused windows, but it does not create an apothecary-specific autonomous callback; the mechanic's only such callback is the full-only grind process already excluded above.
